chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man and Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ammar ibn Marwan, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
Be patient with the enemies of the favours, for you will not recompense the one who disobeys Allah regarding you with anything superior to obeying Allah regarding him.

key_terms.أَعْدَاءِ النِّعَمِ: Enemies of the favours (those who are ungrateful for blessings)

ai.seo_question: What is the best way to respond to ungrateful people according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the optimal response to the ingratitude of 'enemies of blessings' (a'da' al-ni'am) as maintaining divine obedience, thereby transforming personal patience into a spiritual victory. This teaching underscores the Shia concept of 'i'tidal' (balance), where one's reward is measured not by the recipient's reaction but by the fidelity of one's own worship, a principle deeply rooted in the ethical framework of the Ahl al-Bayt. It serves as a practical guide for navigating social and familial tensions with grace, ensuring that the giver's intent remains pure and aligned with Allah's pleasure.
